column1: # SUPERSEDED FOR THIS LETTER (28 Sept 2026, campaign steps H6/H35): the image this table was read from, Tomokiyo's spinelly1515.png, is his
# reconstruction of Spinelly's ENGLISH DIPLOMATIC cipher (Cotton MS Galba B III, 1512-1515; henryvii.htm 'Notes added in August 2023'),
# not the brothers' private cipher. The brothers' key is Domnina's (2015 Fig. 1, corrected 2016): sources/domnina-2015-2016/ and
# keys/key_domnina_2016_atlasmap*.tsv. Kept as the record of what H1-H34 tested against.
# Spinelly's cipher (Thomas/Leonardo Spinelli brothers' private correspondence, from about 3 Jan 1515),
# a homophonic substitution cipher with some nulls (Ekaterina Domnina, "Ciphers in Early Tudor Diplomacy",
# Geheime Post (2015), p.185, Fig.1 -- per Tomokiyo's henryvii.htm citation). Domnina's own PDF
# (istina.msu.ru, linked from henryvii.htm as "updated pdf") 404s as of 27 Sept 2026 (INTAKE-SPINELLI,
# this job's one allowed request to that host) -- her Fig.1 image itself could not be fetched or checked
# this job. The table transcribed below is instead Tomokiyo's OWN independently published reconstruction
# of the same cipher, image spinelly1515.png, embedded in henryvii.htm under "Notes added in August 2023:
# Spinelly's cipher can be reconstructed as follows." -- credited to him, not to Domnina, since his image
# is what was actually available and read (same substitution as INTAKE-4715-F61 used Tomokiyo's own
# mayenne.png rather than a period original). A future worker with access to Domnina's Fig.1 (p.185) should
# cross-check this table against hers before relying on it for anything beyond calibration.
# Transcribed INTAKE-SPINELLI, 27 Sept 2026, from sources/cryptiana/web/img/spinelly1515.png (fetched from
# cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/, see sources/cryptiana/README.md), by two independent blind Sonnet subagent
# reads (each shown only the image, no context beyond the table's own printed column headers, asked for a
# literal ink-shape description per cell, not a letter guess), followed by this worker's own zoomed/cropped
# re-examination of every cell at 3-6x (column boundaries located mechanically from the header row's white-
# pixel runs, not eyeballed) -- the crop pass is what actually settled the columns past "p" and the null/
# word-code counts, where both blind passes had low confidence or reported "no ink visible" for cells this
# worker's own crop found ink in (or correctly found blank).  "sign" describes the hand-drawn mark's shape
# (glyphs cannot be typed). Grade AB = both blind passes substantively agreed on the shape (allowing
# paraphrase) and this worker's crop confirms it; grade M = the blind passes disagreed, were low-confidence,
# or missed the mark entirely, and this worker's own crop settled it; grade ? = a stroke-count or shape
# detail that even this worker's crop could not fully resolve (noted per row).
# Design, per the table image's own printed headers and this worker's crop-based reconstruction (not
# stated in words anywhere on henryvii.htm itself -- the "homophonic... with some nulls" description is
# Domnina's, quoted by Tomokiyo, p.185): 23 plaintext-letter columns in a single row, a b c d e f g h i k l
# m n o p q r s t u x y z (the period Italian/Latin set omitting j, v, w). Three of those 23 columns (q, x,
# z) are BLANK in this reconstruction -- no symbol drawn, confirmed by this worker's own zoomed crop, not a
# transcription gap. Five columns (d, i, l, n, t) carry TWO stacked symbols each -- homophones for that one
# letter, not a letter-pair the way ciphers/fr4715-f61-mayenne-1592's Mayenne table stacks two DIFFERENT
# letters per column (flagged so the two tables are not confused). The other 15 non-blank columns (a, b, c,
# e, f, g, h, k, m, o, p, r, s, u, y) carry one symbol each. Separately, a block of null symbols (12 counted
# by this worker's own crop, in three rows of the source image -- 6, then 1 offset, then 5; the two blind
# passes independently reported 10 and 11 and both explicitly flagged their own count as uncertain, so this
# worker's careful crop-based recount is the number of record, not an average of the two guesses) and five
# word-code entries ("I", "of", "Emperor King of Arragon", "Prince of Castile", "new amity") each with one
# symbol, sit to the right of the letter row. H13 correction (28 Sept 2026, campaign runner): the image has SIX word-code
# symbols under the five headers -- 'Emperor King of Arragon' carries two (a 2-with-bar and a 4-with-plus ladder) and
# 'Prince of Castile' carries a capital-H shape with curled serifs; INTAKE's blind passes both counted five and put the
# ladder under 'Prince of Castile'. The 1519 letter's own sign inventory (glyphs/atlas.tsv, 25 codes over 265 signs)
# goes beyond this table: about 48% of its signs (numeral-2 shapes, diamonds, x-crosses, a theta, 'll' pairs, plus
# signs, a bold N) match nothing here, and the shape-for-shape application of this table fails a shuffled-key control
# (NOTES.md, campaign step H4) -- so this table is a period-adjacent reconstruction of the brothers' 1515 cipher, not
# a key that opens the 7 Sept 1519 letter as read. Total hand-drawn symbols: 15 (single letters) + 10 (5 letters
# x2 homophones) + 12 (nulls) + 6 (word codes, H13) = 43.
